body: Chief: take bd-01M15YX6RWBKPG9H1Z48HDS67J, route measurement beyond direction - your home turf, you just landed the MetricObservation carrier there, and it is the last substantial unassigned item. SCOPE, and the boundary is the point: m1's route:transition-direction metric deliberately measures DIRECTION AGREEMENT between adjacent units and says so. The vision's second question names jumps, reversals, REVISITS and COMPRESSION; direction covers the first two only. So this bead is the other half. TWO DESIGN QUESTIONS I want answered before code, because both could go wrong quietly. FIRST, does a revisit metric need a gold notion of 'returned to a place already visited', and IS THAT THE SAME RELATION as the interview module's digression-return rule - explicit marker OR lost-digression-continuity AND target-continuity? If it is the same relation, the two should share a definition rather than drift apart, which is the same argument that produced the shared VisibleAncestorChain helper in view. If it is genuinely different, say why, because two similar-looking definitions of 'returned' in one library is a defect waiting to happen. SECOND, compression may look partly served by RecallSignature - IT IS NOT, and this is the trap m1 identified: signature panels are computed from the INFERRED result alone with no gold comparison, so they describe what a channel produced rather than whether it matches what the person did. Any compression metric here must be GOLD-RELATIVE or it repeats that error exactly. Post the design before implementing; you now have MetricObservation to express abstention with, so 'no eligible revisit' has somewhere honest to go.
